transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well... I suppose I'm just having trouble keeping things in order lately. I can't seem to manage it anymore. 

The kitchen table is just... covered. It's full of my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center... half-finished lists. I just sit there looking at it. I never know which thing to do first, and... well, then the whole day is just gone.
Has this difficulty with organizing and managing your tasks been something you've struggled with your entire life, or is this a more recent change?

No, it's... it's not a recent change. I suppose it's always been this way. 

Even when I was a little girl... my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but careless. I was always forgetting my books, or my homework. They'd always have to remind me to finish my seatwork before I could go outside. So... yes. It's been a long time.
Do you often feel like you are driven by a motor, or do you find it hard to sit still for long periods?
No... I don't think so. I don't have any trouble sitting still. I suppose I sit quite a bit, actually... so, no. That's not really an issue for me.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others when they are talking or blurting out answers before a question has been fully asked?
No... I don't really do that. I usually just listen. I'm not much of a talker, really.
When you are working on a task, do you often find that your mind drifts off and you have trouble staying focused until the work is finished?
I suppose... I'm not really sure. I don't have many big tasks to do these days, so... I haven't really noticed. My mind might wander a bit, I guess, but I haven't paid much attention to it.
Do you often find that you lose things that are necessary for your daily activities, such as your keys, glasses, or important documents?

I suppose I do... yes. I'm always looking for things. It seems like I just had them in my hand... my reading glasses, or the car keys. Sometimes it's appointment cards, or recipes for the church supper... or the folder for the doctor. I just... lose track of them.
